trl_commit.subject: Add a guide for training on AWS Trainium (#7729)

stages.label: 环境与资源
stages.summary: Python/加速器环境、并行度、混合精度、显存策略（vLLM/DeepSpeed/FSDP/LoRA）与输出目录。

stages.label: 模型与参考/教师
stages.summary: 加载策略模型；按需加载参考模型（KL 锚点）、教师模型（蒸馏）或奖励模型。

stages.label: 数据与提示
stages.summary: 把数据集规范成算法要求的列（prompt / chosen+rejected / label / privileged_context），必要时套 chat template。

stages.label: 监督信号
stages.summary: 奖励函数、奖励模型、教师分布或人类偏好标签——把模型行为变成可优化的标量/分布。

stages.label: 采样（rollout）
stages.summary: 当前策略对每个 prompt 生成 1..N 条补全；可用 transformers 或 vLLM 加速，可挂工具/环境做多轮交互。

stages.label: 优势/偏好估计
stages.summary: 由奖励或 log-ratio 算出学习信号：组内相对优势、leave-one-out 基线、偏好对比或教师-学生分布差。

stages.label: 损失与更新
stages.summary: 重要性比裁剪、损失归一化、KL 正则、熵奖励，然后反向传播与优化器步进。

stages.label: 记录与产物
stages.summary: 指标、样例补全、checkpoint、评测与最终模型导出（save_model/push_to_hub）。

families.label: 在线强化学习
families.summary: 训练时用当前策略采样补全，再用奖励函数或奖励模型打分，属于真正的 on-policy RL（GRPO/RLOO/GMPO/SDPO/A*-PO/Async GRPO）。

families.label: 偏好对齐
families.summary: 直接在成对/带标签的偏好数据上做优化，不需要在线采样，也不需要单独的奖励模型（DPO/KTO/ORPO/CPO/TPO/Online DPO）。

families.label: 蒸馏
families.summary: 用教师模型的下一 token 分布监督学生模型，不依赖奖励函数（Distillation/GKD/GOLD/SDFT/IW-OPD）。

families.label: 奖励模型
families.summary: 训练 ORM 奖励模型，产出可被在线 RL 直接调用的打分模型。

families.label: 监督微调
families.summary: RL 之前的冷启动阶段，把模型拉到能稳定产出格式正确的补全。

planes.label: 任务平面
planes.summary: ScriptArguments + DatasetMixtureConfig：数据来源与切分、奖励函数。

planes.label: 模型平面
planes.summary: ModelConfig：模型 id、精度、LoRA 与量化。

algorithms.label: GRPO
algorithms.summary: 对每个 prompt 采样一组（num_generations 条）补全，用组内奖励的相对大小构造优势，去掉 PPO 的价值网络（critic），显存与调参成本大幅下降，是当前开源 RLHF/RLVR 的默认选择。

data.format: prompt（对话列表或纯文本，列名 prompt 可由 remove_unused_columns=False 时的其他列补充）
data.notes: 数据集至少要有 prompt 列；自定义奖励函数还能用到数据集里的任意列（如 answer、test_cases），因此 remove_unused_columns 默认保持 False。

stages.env: TrainingArguments + accelerate 配置（单卡/多卡/DeepSpeed ZeRO-3）；可选 vLLM colocate 或 server 模式加速生成。
stages.model: 策略模型；beta=0.0（默认）时不加载参考模型，显存更省；disable_dropout 保证 logp 可复现。
stages.data: prompt 数据集按 generation_batch_size × steps_per_generation 切分，可 shuffle_dataset。
stages.signal: reward_funcs：内置（accuracy_reward / reasoning_accuracy_reward / think_format_reward / get_soft_overlong_punishment）、任意 dotted path 的 Python 函数，或一个奖励模型路径。
stages.rollout: 每组采样 num_generations 条，max_completion_length 截断，temperature/top_p/top_k/min_p 控制多样性；支持工具调用与 rollout_func 自定义。
stages.estimate: 组内标准化优势：scale_rewards=group 时用组内标准差，读取多奖励时按 reward_weights 聚合（multi_objective_aggregation）。
stages.update: 按 loss_type 选择聚合方式（grpo/dapo/dr_grpo/bnpo/cispo/sapo/luspo/vespo），重要性比裁剪 epsilon/epsilon_high，beta>0 时加 KL 项，可选熵奖励。
stages.output: completion 日志、clip_ratio/entropy/reward 指标、checkpoint 与 save_model/push_to_hub。

loss_type: dapo (默认，token 级归一化，去长度偏置)
dr_grpo (除以常数，Dr. GRPO 去偏)
bnpo (局部 batch 同 token 数归一化)
cispo (裁剪重要性权重而非优势)
luspo (序列级 + 长度缩放，需 importance_sampling_level=sequence)
vespo (Gamma 加权序列级重要性比)

pros: 无需 critic/价值网络，省显存、少一套超参
奖励可以是任意可执行代码（判题、格式检查、规则），RLVR 场景最实用
同一 trainer 通过 loss_type/importance_sampling_level 覆盖 DAPO/GSPO/Dr.GRPO/CISPO/SAPO 等变体
cons: 依赖组内奖励方差：一组全对或全错时优势为 0，没有梯度信号
生成成本高（每题 num_generations 条补全），长 CoT 场景尤其吃显存
奖励函数写错会安静地把模型带偏，必须自己做抽查
pitfalls: 有效 batch（per_device_train_batch_size × num_processes × gradient_accumulation_steps）必须能被 num_generations 整除
beta 默认 0.0：不加 KL 就是纯奖励最大化，模型可能跑偏；需要约束就设 beta>0，代价是要多留一份参考模型显存
num_generations=8 且长补全时，显存需求最高的是生成阶段，先调 max_completion_length 再调 batch
用 vLLM 时 vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 与训练进程共享显存，设太高会 OOM

fields.name: logging_steps
fields.help: Log every X updates steps. Should be an integer or a float in range `[0,1)`. If smaller than 1, will be interpreted as ratio of total training steps.

fields.name: gradient_checkpointing
fields.help: Enable gradient checkpointing to trade compute for memory. Reduces memory at the cost of ~20%% slower training.

fields.name: bf16
fields.help: Whether to use bf16 (mixed) precision instead of 32-bit. Requires Ampere or higher NVIDIA architecture or Intel XPU or using CPU (use_cpu) or Ascend NPU. If not set, it defaults to `True` if `fp16` is not set.

fields.name: lr_scheduler_kwargs
fields.help: Additional parameters for the lr_scheduler, such as {'num_cycles': 1} for cosine with hard restarts. See the documentation of each scheduler for possible values.

fields.name: use_liger_kernel
fields.help: Enable Liger Kernel optimizations: transformers patches the model's layers with Liger's Triton kernels. Deprecated in `SFTTrainer`, `DPOTrainer`, `KTOTrainer`, `GRPOTrainer` and `RLOOTrainer`, and will be removed in v2.0.0: use `model_init_kwargs={"use_kernels": True}` instead.

fields.name: torch_empty_cache_steps
fields.help: Number of steps to wait before calling `torch.<device>.empty_cache()`. Helps avoid CUDA OOM at a cost of ~10%% slower performance. If None, cache will not be emptied.

fields.name: learning_rate
fields.help: The initial learning rate for AdamW.

fields.name: model_init_kwargs
fields.help: Keyword arguments for `transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`, used when the `model` argument of the `GRPOTrainer` is provided as a string. The `revision` value is also used when loading processing classes.
fields.group: Parameters that control the model and reference model

fields.name: trust_remote_code
fields.help: Whether to allow loading models and tokenizers that ship custom Python code from the Hub. Forwarded to `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` and `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`. Also applied to reward-model and reward-tokenizer loads.
fields.group: Parameters that control the model and reference model

fields.name: router_aux_loss_coef
fields.help: Coefficient of the load-balancing auxiliary loss for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, added to the training loss with this weight. When not set, the value declared by the model config is used. Set to `0.0` to disable it. Fails when used with a non-MoE model.
fields.group: Parameters that control the model and reference model

fields.name: disable_dropout
fields.help: Whether to disable dropout in the model. This is useful for training with a reference model, as it prevents the model from generating different logprobs for the same input.
fields.group: Parameters that control the model and reference model

fields.name: cast_lm_head_to_fp32
fields.help: Whether to cast the language modeling head of the policy and reference models to float32. As recommended by the [ScaleRL](https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.13786) recipe. This flag is only supported when the model has untied word embedding and language modeling head layers i.e. `tie_word_embeddings` in the model config is False.
fields.group: Parameters that control the model and reference model

fields.name: remove_unused_columns
fields.help: Whether to only keep the column 'prompt' in the dataset. If you use a custom reward function that requires any column other than 'prompts' and 'completions', you should keep this to `False`.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: num_generations
fields.help: Number of generations to sample. The effective batch size (num_processes * per_device_batch_size * gradient_accumulation_steps) must be evenly divisible by this value.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: num_generations_eval
fields.help: Number of generations to sample during evaluation. This allows using fewer generations during evaluation to save computation. If `None`, uses the value of `num_generations`.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: max_completion_length
fields.help: Maximum length of the generated completion.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: ds3_gather_for_generation
fields.help: This setting applies to DeepSpeed ZeRO-3. If enabled, the policy model weights are gathered for generation, improving generation speed. However, disabling this option allows training models that exceed the VRAM capacity of a single GPU, albeit at the cost of slower generation. Disabling this option is not compatible with vLLM generation.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: shuffle_dataset
fields.help: Whether to shuffle the training dataset.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: pad_to_multiple_of
fields.help: If set, the prompts ids and completions ids will be padded to a multiple of this value. `'auto'` pads to a multiple of 128 on Neuron (AWS Trainium), which compiles once per input shape, and does not pad elsewhere.
fields.group: Parameters that control the data preprocessing

fields.name: generation_batch_size
fields.help: Batch size to use for generation. If `None`, it defaults to the effective training batch size: `per_device_train_batch_size * num_processes * steps_per_generation`.

fields.name: steps_per_generation
fields.help: Number of steps per generation. If `None`, it defaults to `gradient_accumulation_steps`.

fields.name: temperature
fields.help: Temperature for sampling. The higher the temperature, the more random the completions.

fields.name: top_p
fields.help: Float that controls the cumulative probability of the top tokens to consider. Must be in (0, 1]. Set to 1.0 to consider all tokens.

fields.name: top_k
fields.help: Number of highest probability vocabulary tokens to keep for top-k-filtering. If `0`, top-k-filtering is disabled and all tokens are considered.

fields.name: min_p
fields.help: Minimum token probability, which will be scaled by the probability of the most likely token. It must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0. Typical values are in the 0.01-0.2 range.

fields.name: generation_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to `GenerationConfig` (if using transformers) or `SamplingParams` (if using vLLM) when sampling completions. This can be used to further customize the generation behavior, such as setting `suppress_tokens`, `num_beams`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other generation parameters (like `min_p`, `top_p`, etc.), they will override them.

fields.name: chat_template_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to the `apply_chat_template` function when generating completions.

fields.name: repetition_penalty
fields.help: Float that penalizes new tokens based on whether they appear in the prompt and the generated text so far. Values > 1.0 encourage the model to use new tokens, while values < 1.0 encourage the model to repeat tokens.

fields.name: cache_implementation
fields.help: Implementation of the cache method for faster generation when use_vllm is set to False.

fields.name: use_vllm
fields.help: Whether to use vLLM for generating completions. If set to `True`, the trainer will use vLLM for generation instead of the default model.generate(). Requires `vllm` to be installed.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_mode
fields.help: Mode to use for vLLM integration when `use_vllm` is set to `True`. Must be one of `'server'` or `'colocate'`. `'server'`: The trainer will send generation requests to a separate vLLM server. Make sure a vLLM server is running (start with `vllm serve`). `'colocate'`: vLLM will run in the same process and share the training GPUs. This avoids the need for a separate server but may cause resource contention with training.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_model_impl
fields.help: Model implementation to use for vLLM. Must be one of `transformers` or `vllm`. `transformers`: Use the `transformers` backend for model implementation. `vllm`: Use the `vllm` library for model implementation.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_enable_sleep_mode
fields.help: Enable vLLM sleep mode to offload weights/cache during the optimizer step. Keeps GPU memory usage low, but waking the engine adds host–device transfer latency.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_structured_outputs_regex
fields.help: Regex for vLLM structured outputs. If `None` (default), structured outputs is disabled.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_server_base_url
fields.help: Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., 'http://localhost:8000'). If provided, `vllm_server_host` and `vllm_server_port` are ignored.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_host
fields.help: Host of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if vllm_server_base_url is provided.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_port
fields.help: Port of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if vllm_server_base_url is provided.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_timeout
fields.help: Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the vLLM server to be up. If the server is not up after the timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_group_port
fields.help: Port number for the weight update group. This is used to communicate with the vLLM server. Unless the port is occupied, there is no need to change it.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_gpu_memory_utilization
fields.help: Control the GPU memory utilization for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` flag.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: vllm_max_model_length
fields.help: Context window for vLLM. Set it to at least the maximum prompt length in the dataset plus `max_completion_length`; if omitted, it is inferred from the model config.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: vllm_tensor_parallel_size
fields.help: Control the tensor parallel size for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_tensor_parallel_size` flag.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: beta
fields.help: KL coefficient. If `0.0` (default), the reference model is not loaded, reducing memory usage and improving training speed. [DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning](https://huggingface.co/papers/2501.12948) use a value of `0.001`.

fields.name: num_iterations
fields.help: Number of iterations per batch (denoted as μ in the algorithm).

fields.name: epsilon
fields.help: Epsilon value for clipping.

fields.name: delta
fields.help: Enables the upper clipping bound in two-sided GRPO loss when set to a float. If `None` (default), standard GRPO clipping is used. Recommended to be greater than `1 + ε` when enabled. This method is introduced in the [INTELLECT-2 tech report](https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.07291).

fields.name: epsilon_high
fields.help: Upper-bound epsilon value for clipping. If not specified, it defaults to the same value as the lower-bound specified in argument `epsilon`. Paper DAPO recommends `0.28`. When used with `loss_type='cispo'`, this corresponds to the ε_max param specified in the [ScaleRL paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.13786) and the recommended value is `5.0`.

fields.name: sapo_temperature_neg
fields.help: Temperature for tokens with non-positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter is introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).

fields.name: sapo_temperature_pos
fields.help: Temperature for tokens with positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter is introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).

fields.name: vespo_k_pos
fields.help: k parameter for positive advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).

fields.name: vespo_lambda_pos
fields.help: lambda parameter for positive advantages, it is the decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).

fields.name: vespo_k_neg
fields.help: k parameter for negative advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).

fields.name: vespo_lambda_neg
fields.help: lambda parameter for negative advantages, it is the exponential decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).

fields.name: importance_sampling_level
fields.help: Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `'token'` or `'sequence'` level. `'token'` keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `'sequence'` averages the log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The GSPO paper shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more stable training and better alignment with sequence-level rewards.

fields.name: reward_weights
fields.help: Weights for each reward function. Must match the number of reward functions. If `None`, all rewards are weighted equally with weight `1.0`.

fields.name: multi_objective_aggregation
fields.help: Method to aggregate multiple reward functions. Supported values are: `'sum_then_normalize'` (default): First sums the weighted rewards from each reward function, then applies reward scaling/normalization as specified by `scale_rewards` (see `scale_rewards` for details). `'normalize_then_sum'`: First normalizes/scales each reward function across generations (within each group), then sums the normalized rewards using the specified weights. The aggregated reward is then normalized at the batch level when forming advantages. This is the suggested approach from the paper GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization.

fields.name: scale_rewards
fields.help: Specifies the scaling strategy for rewards. Supported values are: `True` or `group'` (default): rewards are scaled by the standard deviation within each group, ensuring unit variance within a group. `'batch'`: rewards are scaled by the standard deviation across the entire batch, as recommended in the PPO Lite paper. `False` or `'none'`: no scaling is applied. The Dr. GRPO paper recommends not scaling rewards, as scaling by the standard deviation introduces a question-level difficulty bias.

fields.name: loss_type
fields.help: Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are 'grpo', 'dr_grpo', 'dapo', 'bnpo', 'cispo', 'sapo', 'luspo', and 'vespo'. 'grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing over sequence length. Not recommended due to length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones with negative advantages. 'dapo' (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the DAPO paper to eliminate length bias. 'dr_grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with a global constant. This method was introduced in the Dr. GRPO paper to eliminate length bias. The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`. 'bnpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the local batch. Note that normalization is performed over the local batch only, so results may slightly vary depending on the local batch size, despite a constant effective batch size. When using `per_device_train_batch_size==1`, the loss is equivalent to the GRPO loss. 'cispo': Clips the importance sampling weights instead of the advantage scaled importance weights. The clipped weights are then multiplied with the advantages and policy model's log probs. Individual token losses are aggregated by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the [MiniMax-M1 paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.13585). 'sapo': Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization loss, as introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347). Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates while preserving useful learning signals. 'luspo': Length-Unbiased Sequence Policy Optimization loss. A sequence-level loss that scales each sequence's loss by its length. This is a modification of GSPO and requires `importance_sampling_level='sequence'`. Introduced in the [LUSPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.05261). 'vespo': Variational Sequence-Level Soft Policy Optimization. Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, asymmetric Gamma weighting function applied directly to sequence-level importance weights. Introduced in the [VESPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.10693).

fields.name: mask_truncated_completions
fields.help: When enabled, truncated completions are excluded from the loss calculation, preventing them from being incorrectly penalized and introducing noise during training. According to the DAPO paper, this is a good practice for training stability.

fields.name: sync_ref_model
fields.help: Whether to synchronize the reference model with the active model every `ref_model_sync_steps` steps, using the `ref_model_mixup_alpha` parameter.

fields.name: ref_model_mixup_alpha
fields.help: α parameter from the TR-DPO paper, which controls the mix between the current policy and the previous reference policy during updates. The reference policy is updated according to the equation: `π_ref = α * π_θ + (1 - α) * π_ref_prev`. To use this parameter, you must set `sync_ref_model=True`.

fields.name: ref_model_sync_steps
fields.help: τ parameter from the TR-DPO paper, which determines how frequently the current policy is synchronized with the reference policy. To use this parameter, you must set `sync_ref_model=True`.

fields.name: top_entropy_quantile
fields.help: ρ parameter from Beyond the 80/20 Rule. Keeps in the policy loss term only the top-ρ quantile of tokens by entropy of the probability distribution at each sequence position, improving results. Range: [0.0-1.0]. A value of `0.0` masks all but the highest entropy token; `1.0` keeps all tokens. The paper recommends a value of `0.2`. If used with `mask_truncated_completions=True`, only tokens from non-truncated completions are considered.

fields.name: entropy_coef
fields.help: Coefficient of the entropy regularization term in the loss. A positive value adds an entropy bonus that encourages exploration. The bonus is always the mean per-token entropy regardless of `loss_type` (not rescaled to a loss type's policy normalization), so `entropy_coef` has the same meaning for every loss type. When `use_adaptive_entropy=True`, this serves as the initial coefficient and is updated each optimizer step. Has no effect when set to `0.0` (default).

fields.name: use_adaptive_entropy
fields.help: Whether to use adaptive entropy control, introduced in Skywork-OR1 (https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.22312). When enabled, `entropy_coef` is incremented by `entropy_coef_delta` when entropy is below `entropy_target`, and decremented otherwise.

fields.name: entropy_coef_min
fields.help: Lower bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_coef_max
fields.help: Upper bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_coef_delta
fields.help: Step size for adjusting the entropy coefficient during adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_target
fields.help: Target mean per-token entropy (nats) for adaptive entropy control. The coefficient is only applied when current entropy is at or below this value. Measured over the same token set as the policy loss (all completion tokens, or the high-entropy subset when top_entropy_quantile < 1.0). Typical language models have per-token entropies of 2–10 nats, so the default of 0.2 almost never triggers regularization (only on near-complete collapse); set it close to the entropy observed early in training and tune from there.

fields.name: max_tool_calling_iterations
fields.help: Maximum number of tool-calling turns when training an agent. If `None`, there is no limit and generation stops when the model generates a response turn with no tool calls or when the total response length reaches `max_model_length`.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_correction

algorithms.label: RLOO
algorithms.summary: REINFORCE 式在线 RL：每个 prompt 采样 k 条补全（num_generations），用“其余 k-1 条的平均奖励”作为 leave-one-out 基线，比组内标准化更温和，并保留 PPO 式序列级概率比裁剪。

data.notes: 与 GRPO 相同的数据契约；默认 num_generations=2，即 k=2。

stages.model: 策略模型；beta=0.05 默认>0，因此默认会加载参考模型（要省显存就设 beta=0.0）。
stages.signal: reward_funcs（内置/自定义/奖励模型），可用 reward_weights 与 reward_clip_range。
stages.rollout: 每个 prompt 采样 num_generations 条补全。
stages.estimate: leave-one-out 基线：优势 = 本样本奖励 − 其余样本平均奖励；不可打分的样本标记为 NaN 并从基线里剔除。可选 normalize_advantages 做批归一化。
stages.update: 序列级重要性比裁剪（epsilon/epsilon_high）后的 REINFORCE 损失，加上 beta 控制的 KL 项。

pros: 比 GRPO 更简单：没有组内标准差、不需要多奖励聚合逻辑
k=2 就能训，生成成本约为 GRPO(num_generations=8) 的 1/4
保留了序列级裁剪，更新幅度可控
cons: 基线方差比组标准化 GRPO 稍大，奖励噪声大时更抖
不支持工具调用/多轮交互（GRPOTrainer 才支持）
同样受“全对/全错组无梯度”的影响
pitfalls: 论文里的 RLOO 不含 KL，但 TRL 默认 beta=0.05；要复现论文设 beta=0.0
num_generations 就是论文中的 k，调大能降方差但线性增加生成成本

algorithms.summary: GRPO 的变体：把 token 级重要性比的算术平均换成几何平均，几何平均对离群比值远不敏感，因此可以用比 GRPO 大得多的裁剪区间而保持稳定。

cons: 几何平均需要对负数/零比值做保护，实现细节影响结果
实验命名空间，API 可能变动

fields.help: Number of highest probability vocabulary tokens to keep for top-k-filtering. If `0`, top-k-filtering is disabled and all tokens are considered.

fields.name: min_p
fields.help: Minimum token probability, which will be scaled by the probability of the most likely token. It must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0. Typical values are in the 0.01-0.2 range.

fields.name: generation_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to `GenerationConfig` (if using transformers) or `SamplingParams` (if using vLLM) when sampling completions. This can be used to further customize the generation behavior, such as setting `suppress_tokens`, `num_beams`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other generation parameters (like `min_p`, `top_p`, etc.), they will override them.

fields.name: chat_template_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to the `apply_chat_template` function when generating completions.

fields.name: repetition_penalty
fields.help: Float that penalizes new tokens based on whether they appear in the prompt and the generated text so far. Values > 1.0 encourage the model to use new tokens, while values < 1.0 encourage the model to repeat tokens.

fields.name: cache_implementation
fields.help: Implementation of the cache method for faster generation when use_vllm is set to False.

fields.name: use_vllm
fields.help: Whether to use vLLM for generating completions. If set to `True`, the trainer will use vLLM for generation instead of the default model.generate(). Requires `vllm` to be installed.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_mode
fields.help: Mode to use for vLLM integration when `use_vllm` is set to `True`. Must be one of `'server'` or `'colocate'`. `'server'`: The trainer will send generation requests to a separate vLLM server. Make sure a vLLM server is running (start with `vllm serve`). `'colocate'`: vLLM will run in the same process and share the training GPUs. This avoids the need for a separate server but may cause resource contention with training.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_model_impl
fields.help: Model implementation to use for vLLM. Must be one of `transformers` or `vllm`. `transformers`: Use the `transformers` backend for model implementation. `vllm`: Use the `vllm` library for model implementation.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_enable_sleep_mode
fields.help: Enable vLLM sleep mode to offload weights/cache during the optimizer step. Keeps GPU memory usage low, but waking the engine adds host–device transfer latency.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_structured_outputs_regex
fields.help: Regex for vLLM structured outputs. If `None` (default), structured outputs is disabled.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by vLLM

fields.name: vllm_server_base_url
fields.help: Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., 'http://localhost:8000'). If provided, `vllm_server_host` and `vllm_server_port` are ignored.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_host
fields.help: Host of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if vllm_server_base_url is provided.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_port
fields.help: Port of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if vllm_server_base_url is provided.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_server_timeout
fields.help: Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the vLLM server to be up. If the server is not up after the timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_group_port
fields.help: Port number for the weight update group. This is used to communicate with the vLLM server. Unless the port is occupied, there is no need to change it.
fields.group: Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)

fields.name: vllm_gpu_memory_utilization
fields.help: Control the GPU memory utilization for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` flag.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: vllm_max_model_length
fields.help: Context window for vLLM. Set it to at least the maximum prompt length in the dataset plus `max_completion_length`; if omitted, it is inferred from the model config.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: vllm_tensor_parallel_size
fields.help: Control the tensor parallel size for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_tensor_parallel_size` flag.
fields.group: Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)

fields.name: beta
fields.help: KL coefficient. If `0.0` (default), the reference model is not loaded, reducing memory usage and improving training speed. [DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning](https://huggingface.co/papers/2501.12948) use a value of `0.001`.

fields.name: num_iterations
fields.help: Number of iterations per batch (denoted as μ in the algorithm).

fields.name: epsilon
fields.help: Lower-bound clipping value, expressed in log space. The lower bound of the per-token importance ratio is exp(-epsilon). GMPO recommends 0.4.

fields.name: delta
fields.help: Enables the upper clipping bound in two-sided GRPO loss when set to a float. If `None` (default), standard GRPO clipping is used. Recommended to be greater than `1 + ε` when enabled. This method is introduced in the [INTELLECT-2 tech report](https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.07291).

fields.name: epsilon_high
fields.help: Upper-bound epsilon value for clipping. If not specified, it defaults to the same value as the lower-bound specified in argument `epsilon`. Paper DAPO recommends `0.28`. When used with `loss_type='cispo'`, this corresponds to the ε_max param specified in the [ScaleRL paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.13786) and the recommended value is `5.0`.

fields.name: sapo_temperature_neg
fields.help: Temperature for tokens with non-positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter is introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).

fields.name: sapo_temperature_pos
fields.help: Temperature for tokens with positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter is introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).

fields.name: vespo_k_pos
fields.help: k parameter for positive advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).

fields.name: vespo_lambda_pos
fields.help: lambda parameter for positive advantages, it is the decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).

fields.name: vespo_k_neg
fields.help: k parameter for negative advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).

fields.name: vespo_lambda_neg
fields.help: lambda parameter for negative advantages, it is the exponential decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).

fields.name: importance_sampling_level
fields.help: Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `'token'` or `'sequence'` level. `'token'` keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `'sequence'` averages the log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The GSPO paper shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more stable training and better alignment with sequence-level rewards.

fields.name: reward_weights
fields.help: Weights for each reward function. Must match the number of reward functions. If `None`, all rewards are weighted equally with weight `1.0`.

fields.name: multi_objective_aggregation
fields.help: Method to aggregate multiple reward functions. Supported values are: `'sum_then_normalize'` (default): First sums the weighted rewards from each reward function, then applies reward scaling/normalization as specified by `scale_rewards` (see `scale_rewards` for details). `'normalize_then_sum'`: First normalizes/scales each reward function across generations (within each group), then sums the normalized rewards using the specified weights. The aggregated reward is then normalized at the batch level when forming advantages. This is the suggested approach from the paper GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization.

fields.name: scale_rewards
fields.help: Specifies the scaling strategy for rewards. Supported values are: `True` or `group'` (default): rewards are scaled by the standard deviation within each group, ensuring unit variance within a group. `'batch'`: rewards are scaled by the standard deviation across the entire batch, as recommended in the PPO Lite paper. `False` or `'none'`: no scaling is applied. The Dr. GRPO paper recommends not scaling rewards, as scaling by the standard deviation introduces a question-level difficulty bias.

fields.name: loss_type
fields.help: Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are 'grpo', 'dr_grpo', 'dapo', 'bnpo', 'cispo', 'sapo', 'luspo', and 'vespo'. 'grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing over sequence length. Not recommended due to length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones with negative advantages. 'dapo' (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the DAPO paper to eliminate length bias. 'dr_grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with a global constant. This method was introduced in the Dr. GRPO paper to eliminate length bias. The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`. 'bnpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the local batch. Note that normalization is performed over the local batch only, so results may slightly vary depending on the local batch size, despite a constant effective batch size. When using `per_device_train_batch_size==1`, the loss is equivalent to the GRPO loss. 'cispo': Clips the importance sampling weights instead of the advantage scaled importance weights. The clipped weights are then multiplied with the advantages and policy model's log probs. Individual token losses are aggregated by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the [MiniMax-M1 paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.13585). 'sapo': Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization loss, as introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347). Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates while preserving useful learning signals. 'luspo': Length-Unbiased Sequence Policy Optimization loss. A sequence-level loss that scales each sequence's loss by its length. This is a modification of GSPO and requires `importance_sampling_level='sequence'`. Introduced in the [LUSPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.05261). 'vespo': Variational Sequence-Level Soft Policy Optimization. Replaces hard clipping with a smooth, asymmetric Gamma weighting function applied directly to sequence-level importance weights. Introduced in the [VESPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.10693).

fields.name: mask_truncated_completions
fields.help: When enabled, truncated completions are excluded from the loss calculation, preventing them from being incorrectly penalized and introducing noise during training. According to the DAPO paper, this is a good practice for training stability.

fields.name: sync_ref_model
fields.help: Whether to synchronize the reference model with the active model every `ref_model_sync_steps` steps, using the `ref_model_mixup_alpha` parameter.

fields.name: ref_model_mixup_alpha
fields.help: α parameter from the TR-DPO paper, which controls the mix between the current policy and the previous reference policy during updates. The reference policy is updated according to the equation: `π_ref = α * π_θ + (1 - α) * π_ref_prev`. To use this parameter, you must set `sync_ref_model=True`.

fields.name: ref_model_sync_steps
fields.help: τ parameter from the TR-DPO paper, which determines how frequently the current policy is synchronized with the reference policy. To use this parameter, you must set `sync_ref_model=True`.

fields.name: top_entropy_quantile
fields.help: ρ parameter from Beyond the 80/20 Rule. Keeps in the policy loss term only the top-ρ quantile of tokens by entropy of the probability distribution at each sequence position, improving results. Range: [0.0-1.0]. A value of `0.0` masks all but the highest entropy token; `1.0` keeps all tokens. The paper recommends a value of `0.2`. If used with `mask_truncated_completions=True`, only tokens from non-truncated completions are considered.

fields.name: entropy_coef
fields.help: Coefficient of the entropy regularization term in the loss. A positive value adds an entropy bonus that encourages exploration. The bonus is always the mean per-token entropy regardless of `loss_type` (not rescaled to a loss type's policy normalization), so `entropy_coef` has the same meaning for every loss type. When `use_adaptive_entropy=True`, this serves as the initial coefficient and is updated each optimizer step. Has no effect when set to `0.0` (default).

fields.name: use_adaptive_entropy
fields.help: Whether to use adaptive entropy control, introduced in Skywork-OR1 (https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.22312). When enabled, `entropy_coef` is incremented by `entropy_coef_delta` when entropy is below `entropy_target`, and decremented otherwise.

fields.name: entropy_coef_min
fields.help: Lower bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_coef_max
fields.help: Upper bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_coef_delta
fields.help: Step size for adjusting the entropy coefficient during adaptive entropy control.

fields.name: entropy_target
fields.help: Target mean per-token entropy (nats) for adaptive entropy control. The coefficient is only applied when current entropy is at or below this value. Measured over the same token set as the policy loss (all completion tokens, or the high-entropy subset when top_entropy_quantile < 1.0). Typical language models have per-token entropies of 2–10 nats, so the default of 0.2 almost never triggers regularization (only on near-complete collapse); set it close to the entropy observed early in training and tune from there.

fields.name: max_tool_calling_iterations
fields.help: Maximum number of tool-calling turns when training an agent. If `None`, there is no limit and generation stops when the model generates a response turn with no tool calls or when the total response length reaches `max_model_length`.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_correction
fields.help: Whether to apply Importance Sampling (IS) to correct for the mismatch between vLLM completion logprobs and recomputed training logprobs. If set to `False`, no IS is applied regardless of `vllm_importance_sampling_mode`. When `True`, the selected mode determines how IS ratios are computed and constrained.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_mode
fields.help: Specifies how Importance Sampling (IS) is performed when vllm_importance_sampling_correction=True. Modes are defined along two orthogonal dimensions: (1) constraint, which determines how to handle ratios outside the bounds [C_min, C_max]—either truncation (clip to range, ρ ← clamp(ρ, C_min, C_max)) or masking (set ratios above C_max or below C_min to zero); and (2) granularity, which determines whether ratios are computed per token or as a single sequence-level ratio applied to all tokens. Supported options are: 'token_truncate', 'token_mask', 'sequence_truncate', and 'sequence_mask'.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_clip_max
fields.help: Importance sampling upper bound C_max used by `vllm_importance_sampling_mode`. For '*_truncate' modes, ratios are clipped from above at C_max. For '*_mask' modes, ratios larger than C_max are set to zero.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_clip_min
fields.help: Importance sampling lower bound C_min used by `vllm_importance_sampling_mode`. For `*_truncate` modes, ratios are clipped from below at C_min. For `*_mask` modes, ratios below C_min are set to zero. To strictly mask ratios below C_min without upper bound, set `vllm_importance_sampling_clip_max=None`.

fields.name: off_policy_mask_threshold
fields.help: Threshold for off-policy sequence masking. If `None`, off-policy sequence masking is disabled. When set, sequences with negative advantages and high KL divergence are masked out to stabilize training. This parameter corresponds to the `delta` threshold in Equation 9 of the [DeepSeek-V3.2 paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2512.02556). It expects a positive value (e.g., 0.5).

fields.name: use_bias_correction_kl
fields.help: Whether to multiply the KL term by the importance sampling ratio, so that the KL gradient becomes the unbiased reverse-KL gradient, as described in the [DeepSeek-V3.2 paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2512.02556). This changes the KL gradient whenever `beta != 0`, including on-policy: the ratio is differentiable, so it affects the gradient even where its value is exactly 1. The unbiased reverse-KL property holds for `importance_sampling_level='token'`; with 'sequence' a sequence-level weight is broadcast onto the per-token KL.

fields.name: log_completions
fields.help: Whether to log a sample of (prompt, completion) pairs every `logging_steps` steps. If `rich` is installed, it prints the sample. If `wandb` logging is enabled, it logs it to `wandb`.

fields.name: log_multimodal
fields.help: Whether to log multimodal content (images, videos, etc.) together with completions. Disable this to reduce log size when using high-resolution multimodal data.

fields.name: num_completions_to_print
fields.help: Number of completions to print with `rich`. If `None`, all completions are logged.

fields.name: log_unique_prompts
fields.help: Whether to log unique prompts. If `True`, only unique prompts are logged. If `False`, all prompts are logged.

fields.name: log_completions_hub_repo
fields.help: Hugging Face Hub repository to save the completions. Should be a complete repository name like `'username/reponame'` or `'orgname/reponame'`, or just `'reponame'` in which case the repository will be created in the currently-logged-in Hugging Face user's namespace. Note that this repository will be public unless you set `hub_private_repo=True` or your organization's default is to create private repositories.

fields.name: use_transformers_continuous_batching
fields.help: Whether to use transformers' continuous batching engine for generating completions. Requires transformers>=5.8.0.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by transformers continuous batching

fields.name: transformers_continuous_batching_config
fields.help: Keyword arguments for `transformers.generation.ContinuousBatchingConfig`.
fields.group: Parameters that control generation acceleration powered by transformers continuous batching

fields.name: use_transformers_paged
fields.help: Deprecated. Use `use_transformers_continuous_batching` instead.

fields.name: vllm_importance_sampling_cap
fields.help: Deprecated, use `vllm_importance_sampling_clip_max` instead. Importance sampling cap C used by `vllm_importance_sampling_mode`. For '*_truncate' modes, ratios are clipped from above at C. For '*_mask' modes, ratios larger than C are set to zero.

algorithms.label: SDPO
algorithms.summary: 在 on-policy 优化之外，把自己高奖励轨迹（或环境反馈）当作“自我教师”，把带反馈条件下的下一 token 预测蒸馏回策略，从而把稀疏的奖励信号变成密集的 token 级学习信号。

stages.model: 策略模型 + 自我教师（teacher_model_kind、teacher_update_rate、teacher_sync_steps）。
stages.signal: reward_funcs 决定哪些轨迹算“成功”（success_reward_threshold）。
stages.rollout: 采样 num_generations 条，可选重提示（max_reprompt_len、dont_reprompt_on_self_success）。
stages.estimate: 奖励优势 + 自我蒸馏的 token 级权重（distillation_weight、distillation_topk）。
stages.update: PPO 式裁剪（epsilon/epsilon_high、importance_sampling_level）与蒸馏损失相加，beta 控制 KL。
stages.output: 同 GRPO，另有 flat-region 诊断指标。

pros: 把稀疏奖励变成密集 token 信号，长 CoT 场景收敛更快
不需要外部教师模型
cons: 字段最多（63 个），配置面广、调参成本高
自我教师可能放大自己的错误
pitfalls: distillation_* 与 GRPO 的 loss_type 同时生效，两组超参要一起调
实验命名空间

fields.name: logging_steps
fields.help: Log every X updates steps. Should be an integer or a float in range `[0,1)`. If smaller than 1, will be interpreted as ratio of total training steps.

fields.name: gradient_checkpointing
fields.help: Enable gradient checkpointing to trade compute for memory. Reduces memory at the cost of ~20%% slower training.

fields.name: bf16
fields.help: Whether to use bf16 (mixed) precision instead of 32-bit. Requires Ampere or higher NVIDIA architecture or Intel XPU or using CPU (use_cpu) or Ascend NPU. If not set, it defaults to `True` if `fp16` is not set.

fields.name: lr_scheduler_kwargs
fields.help: Additional parameters for the lr_scheduler, such as {'num_cycles': 1} for cosine with hard restarts. See the documentation of each scheduler for possible values.

fields.name: use_liger_kernel
fields.help: Enable Liger Kernel optimizations: transformers patches the model's layers with Liger's Triton kernels. Deprecated in `SFTTrainer`, `DPOTrainer`, `KTOTrainer`, `GRPOTrainer` and `RLOOTrainer`, and will be removed in v2.0.0: use `model_init_kwargs={"use_kernels": True}` instead.

fields.name: torch_empty_cache_steps
fields.help: Number of steps to wait before calling `torch.<device>.empty_cache()`. Helps avoid CUDA OOM at a cost of ~10%% slower performance. If None, cache will not be emptied.

fields.name: model_init_kwargs
fields.help: Keyword arguments for `transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`, used when the `model` argument of the `SDPOTrainer` is provided as a string. The `revision` value is also used when loading processing classes.

fields.name: trust_remote_code
fields.help: Whether to allow loading models and tokenizers that ship custom Python code from the Hub. Forwarded to `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` and `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`. Also applied to reward-model and reward-tokenizer loads.

fields.name: disable_dropout
fields.help: Whether to disable dropout in the model. This is useful for training with a reference model, as it prevents the model from generating different logprobs for the same input.

fields.name: remove_unused_columns
fields.help: Whether to only keep the column 'prompt' in the dataset. If you use a custom reward function that requires any column other than 'prompts' and 'completions', you should keep this to `False`.

fields.name: max_prompt_length
fields.help: Maximum prompt length. Longer prompts are truncated from the left.

fields.name: num_generations
fields.help: Number of generations to sample. The effective batch size (num_processes * per_device_batch_size * gradient_accumulation_steps) must be evenly divisible by this value.

fields.name: num_generations_eval
fields.help: Number of generations to sample during evaluation. This allows using fewer generations during evaluation to save computation. If `None`, uses the value of `num_generations`.

fields.name: max_completion_length
fields.help: Maximum length of the generated completion.

fields.name: ds3_gather_for_generation
fields.help: This setting applies to DeepSpeed ZeRO-3. If enabled, the policy model weights are gathered for generation, improving generation speed. However, disabling this option allows training models that exceed the VRAM capacity of a single GPU, albeit at the cost of slower generation. Disabling this option is not compatible with vLLM generation.

fields.name: shuffle_dataset
fields.help: Whether to shuffle the training dataset.

fields.name: generation_batch_size
fields.help: Batch size to use for generation. If `None`, it defaults to the effective training batch size: `per_device_train_batch_size * num_processes * steps_per_generation`.

fields.name: steps_per_generation
fields.help: Number of steps per generation. If `None`, it defaults to `gradient_accumulation_steps`.

fields.name: temperature
fields.help: Temperature for sampling. The higher the temperature, the more random the completions.

fields.name: top_p
fields.help: Float that controls the cumulative probability of the top tokens to consider. Must be in (0, 1]. Set to 1.0 to consider all tokens.

fields.name: top_k
fields.help: Number of highest probability vocabulary tokens to keep for top-k-filtering. If `0`, top-k-filtering is disabled and all tokens are considered.

fields.name: min_p
fields.help: Minimum token probability, which will be scaled by the probability of the most likely token. It must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0. Typical values are in the 0.01-0.2 range.

fields.name: generation_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to `GenerationConfig` (if using transformers) or `SamplingParams` (if using vLLM) when sampling completions. This can be used to further customize the generation behavior, such as setting `suppress_tokens`, `num_beams`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other generation parameters (like `min_p`, `top_p`, etc.), they will override them.

fields.name: chat_template_kwargs
fields.help: Additional keyword arguments to pass to the `apply_chat_template` function when generating completions.

fields.name: repetition_penalty
fields.help: Float that penalizes new tokens based on whether they appear in the prompt and the generated text so far. Values > 1.0 encourage the model to use new tokens, while values < 1.0 encourage the model to repeat tokens.

fields.name: cache_implementation
fields.help: Implementation of the cache method for faster generation when use_vllm is set to False.

fields.name: use_vllm
fields.help: Whether to use vLLM for generating completions. If set to `True`, the trainer will use vLLM for generation instead of the default model.generate(). Requires `vllm` to be installed.

fields.name: use_teacher_server
fields.help: Compute teacher logprobs from the running vLLM generation server instead of a local teacher forward. Only supported for `teacher_model_kind='live'` with `use_vllm=True`, `vllm_mode='server'`, `distillation_weight=1.0` (pure distillation), and `distillation_mode` in {'sampled_token', 'topk_logits'} (the server returns the teacher's top-k logprobs, not the full vocabulary; `topk_logits` distills over the teacher's own top-k support).

fields.name: vllm_mode
fields.help: Mode to use for vLLM integration when `use_vllm` is set to `True`. Must be one of `'server'` or `'colocate'`. `'server'`: The trainer will send generation requests to a separate vLLM server. Make sure a vLLM server is running (start with `vllm serve`). `'colocate'`: vLLM will run in the same process and share the training GPUs. This avoids the need for a separate server but may cause resource contention with training.

fields.name: vllm_model_impl
fields.help: Model implementation to use for vLLM. Must be one of `transformers` or `vllm`. `transformers`: Use the `transformers` backend for model implementation. `vllm`: Use the `vllm` library for model implementation.

fields.name: vllm_enable_sleep_mode

fields.help: Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., 'http://localhost:8000'). If provided, `vllm_server_host` and `vllm_server_port` are ignored.

fields.name: vllm_tensor_parallel_size
fields.help: Control the tensor parallel size for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_tensor_parallel_size` flag.

fields.name: vllm_gpu_memory_utilization
fields.help: Control the GPU memory utilization for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to `'colocate'`. If you are using `vllm_mode='server'`, this parameter must be passed separately when launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` flag.

fields.name: vllm_max_model_length
fields.help: Context window for vLLM. Set it to at least the maximum prompt length in the dataset plus `max_completion_length`; if omitted, it is inferred from the model config.

fields.name: num_iterations
fields.help: Number of iterations per batch (denoted as μ in the algorithm).

fields.name: loss_type
fields.help: Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are 'grpo', 'bnpo', 'dr_grpo', and 'dapo'. 'grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing over sequence length. Not recommended due to length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones with negative advantages. 'dapo' (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the DAPO paper to eliminate length bias. 'dr_grpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with a global constant. This method was introduced in the Dr. GRPO paper to eliminate length bias. The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`. 'bnpo': Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the local batch. Note that normalization is performed over the local batch only, so results may slightly vary depending on the local batch size, despite a constant effective batch size. When using `per_device_train_batch_size==1`, the loss is equivalent to the GRPO loss.

fields.name: mask_truncated_completions
fields.help: When enabled, truncated completions are excluded from the loss calculation, preventing them from being incorrectly penalized and introducing noise during training. According to the DAPO paper, this is a good practice for training stability.

fields.name: dont_reprompt_on_self_success
fields.help: Skip reprompting when model generates correct response.

fields.name: beta
fields.help: KL coefficient. If `0.0` (default), the reference model is not loaded, reducing memory usage and improving training speed. [DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning](https://huggingface.co/papers/2501.12948) use a value of `0.001`.

fields.name: importance_sampling_level
fields.help: Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `'token'` or `'sequence'` level. `'token'` keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `'sequence'` averages the log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The GSPO paper shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more stable training and better alignment with sequence-level rewards.

fields.name: reward_weights

fields.name: scale_rewards
fields.help: Specifies the scaling strategy for rewards. Supported values are: `True` or `'group'` (default): rewards are scaled by the standard deviation within each group, ensuring unit variance within a group. `'batch'`: rewards are scaled by the standard deviation across the entire batch, as recommended in the PPO Lite paper. `False` or `'none'`: no scaling is applied. The Dr. GRPO paper recommends not scaling rewards, as scaling by the standard deviation introduces a question-level difficulty bias.

fields.name: distillation_alpha
fields.help: Divergence interpolation coefficient. Sampled-token SDPO requires the official reverse-KL setting `distillation_alpha=1.0`.
fields.group: Parameters that control the SDPO loss

fields.name: distillation_mode
fields.help: Distillation objective mode. `sampled_token` is the default SDPO mode and requires `distillation_alpha=1.0`.
fields.group: Parameters that control the SDPO loss

fields.name: distillation_topk
fields.help: Top-k approximation for logit-level SDPO. Must be set when `distillation_mode=topk_logits` and left unset otherwise.
fields.group: Parameters that control the SDPO loss

fields.name: distillation_is_clip
fields.help: Clipping coefficient for importance sampling in self-distillation. `None` disables clipping.
fields.group: Parameters that control the SDPO loss

fields.name: distillation_add_tail
fields.help: Whether to add a tail bucket for non-top-k probability mass.
fields.group: Parameters that control the SDPO loss

fields.name: distillation_weight
fields.help: Convex combination weight between the policy and self-distillation objectives. The loss is `(1 - distillation_weight) * policy_loss + distillation_weight * distillation_loss`. Must be in `[0, 1]`. `1.0` (default) trains purely on self-distillation, `0.0` falls back to the standard GRPO-style policy gradient, and intermediate values blend both.

algorithms.label: A*-PO
algorithms.summary: 两阶段：先用参考策略对每个 prompt 采 num_value_samples 条补全并打分，离线估计最优价值 V*（log-sum-exp 形式并缓存），训练时每个 prompt 只生成 1 条补全，回归到该价值——把在线采样成本压到最低。

data.notes: 第一阶段要对整个数据集采样打分，预处理成本高。

stages.model: 策略模型 + 参考策略（估计 V* 用）。
stages.data: prompt；可 filter_all_incorrect 过滤全错样本。
stages.signal: reward_funcs。
stages.rollout: 阶段一：每个 prompt 采 num_value_samples 条；阶段二：每个 prompt 1 条。
stages.estimate: V*(x)=beta1·log(mean exp(r/beta1))，按 prompt 缓存。
stages.update: 隐式奖励 beta2·log(pi/pi_ref) 与 V* 的平方误差回归。

pros: 训练阶段每题只生成 1 条补全，生成成本极低
离线价值估计可复用
cons: 需要先跑一遍全量采样，冷启动慢
两个 beta 分别控制价值平滑与隐式奖励，耦合较隐蔽
pitfalls: num_value_samples 越大 V* 越准，第一阶段耗时线性增长

algorithms.label: Async GRPO

launch.example: 需要外置 vLLM server 作为 rollout worker

algorithms.summary: 与 GRPO 同一算法，但把生成与训练解耦：后台 worker 持续从 vLLM server 流式产出补全，训练循环只消费，生成与梯度更新重叠执行，吞吐显著提升；代价是数据可能过期（off-policy）。

data.format: prompt（也用 token_budget 控制流水线投喂量）

stages.env: 必须有一个可访问的 vLLM server（vllm_server_base_url）；token_budget/queue_maxsize/max_inflight_tasks 控制流水线水位。
stages.model: 策略模型 + 权重同步（weight_sync_steps/weight_sync_timeout）。
stages.signal: reward_funcs。
stages.rollout: 后台 worker 持续生成，max_staleness 限制数据新鲜度。
stages.estimate: 同 GRPO 的组内相对优势。
stages.update: 裁剪（epsilon/epsilon_high）+ 可选 KL。
stages.output: 吞吐/水位/过期样本等异步指标。

pros: 生成与训练重叠，GPU 利用率高
适合长补全/大规模训练
cons: 必须自建 vLLM server，运维复杂度上升
off-policy 程度由 max_staleness 决定，调不好会掉点
pitfalls: max_staleness 过大 → 训练数据与当前策略差距过大，梯度有偏

algorithms.label: DPO
algorithms.summary: 把 RLHF 的目标改写成对“chosen/rejected”成对样本的分类损失：奖励被隐含在策略与参考策略的对数比里，因此不需要采样、不需要奖励模型，训练稳定、成本低。

data.format: prompt + chosen + rejected（对话格式或纯文本；也支持隐式 prompt / 成对不带 prompt）
data.notes: TRL 会做数据检查与自动 unpair（unpair_preference_dataset）。

stages.model: 策略模型 + 参考模型（ref_model 或隐式 copy）；disable_dropout 默认 True。
stages.data: 成对偏好数据，max_length/truncation_mode 控制截断，padding_free 可省显存。
stages.signal: 人类/AI 偏好标签本身即监督信号；可用 loss_weights 组合多种损失。
stages.rollout: 无（离线），因此训练速度取决于前向次数而非生成。
stages.estimate: chosen/rejected 的隐式奖励差 beta·(log π/π_ref)，logits 由 _precompute_ref_log_probs 预计算缓存。
stages.update: 由 loss_type 决定（sigmoid/hinge/ipo/exo_pair/nca_pair/robust/bco_pair/sppo_hard/aot/apo_zero/apo_down/discopop/sft/sigmoid_norm），可选 label_smoothing、f_divergence 正则。

pros: 不用采样、不用奖励模型，单卡也能跑
有大量可以复现的公开配方与数据
损失函数族覆盖 IPO/CPO/SimPO 思想等变体
cons: 离线偏好数据决定了上限，无法自我探索
对数据质量与分布极敏感，容易学到表面风格
beta 与 loss_type 组合多，需要实验
pitfalls: beta 默认 0.1，改小会让模型偏离参考更远（更激进），改大则几乎不学习
precompute_ref_log_probs=True 可以大幅省显存但会多一遍全量前向
chosen/rejected 必须在同一 tokenizer 下编码，长度截断策略要与数据长度匹配

algorithms.label: Distillation
algorithms.summary: 学生在自己的 on-policy 补全上学习教师的下一 token 分布，用广义 JSD（beta 在 forward KL 与 reverse KL 之间插值）作为目标，不需要奖励函数。

data.format: prompt（也支持 prompt+completion 的混合）

stages.model: 学生模型 + 教师模型（teacher_model_name_or_path，可本地或自定义 init 参数）。
stages.signal: 教师的下一 token 分布（分布级信号，而非标量奖励）。
stages.rollout: 学生生成补全，max_completion_length 控制长度。
stages.estimate: 学生/教师在该补全上的逐 token 分布差（JSD 插值）。
stages.update: 广义 JSD 损失，beta=0 前向 KL、beta=1 反向 KL。
stages.output: 蒸馏损失、perplexity 类指标与 checkpoint。

pros: 不需要奖励函数或偏好数据
分布级信号比标量奖励密集，蒸馏稳定
cons: 必须有教师模型，且要与学生共享 tokenizer（跨 tokenizer 见 GOLD）
生成开销与 RL 相当
pitfalls: 教师模型的 chat template 与学生不同会让分布对齐错位

algorithms.summary: 持续学习场景：学生从普通 prompt 生成，教师是“同一模型 + 特权上下文（privileged_context）”的条件版本，用它重打分来提供 token 级监督，从而在学新知识的同时少遗忘旧能力。

fields.name: beta
fields.help: Interpolation coefficient for the Generalized JSD loss. 0.0 = forward KL, 0.5 = JSD, 1.0 = reverse KL. Unlike GRPO's `beta` (a KL-penalty coefficient against a reference model), here it selects the divergence itself; there is no reference-model KL penalty.

fields.name: max_tool_calling_iterations
fields.help: Maximum number of tool-calling turns when training an agent. If `None`, there is no limit and generation stops when the model generates a response turn with no tool calls or when the total response length reaches `max_model_length`.

fields.name: log_completions
fields.help: Whether to log a sample of (prompt, completion) pairs every `logging_steps` steps. If `rich` is installed, it prints the sample. If `wandb` and/or `trackio` logging is enabled, it logs it to `wandb` and/or `trackio`.

fields.name: num_completions_to_print

fields.name: log_unique_prompts

fields.name: teacher_model_server_url

fields.name: loss_top_k
fields.help: Number of top tokens the teacher server returns and over which the divergence is computed. For beta == 0 this must be positive; for beta > 0 it must be 1.

fields.name: loss_add_tail
fields.help: Whether to append a tail bucket representing the remaining probability mass outside the selected top-k support.

fields.name: reverse_kl_top_1_mode
fields.help: Reverse-KL top-1 token selection when beta > 0 and loss_top_k == 1. Use 'sampled' for the actual completion token or 'argmax' for the student's top-1 token. The forward-KL support always uses the teacher's top-1 token.

algorithms.label: Reward

奖励作弊（reward hacking）风险由下游 RL 承担

fields.name: gradient_checkpointing

fields.name: bf16
fields.help: Whether to use bf16 (mixed) precision instead of 32-bit. Requires Ampere or higher NVIDIA architecture or Intel XPU or using CPU (use_cpu) or Ascend NPU. If not set, it defaults to `True` if `fp16` is not set.

fields.name: lr_scheduler_kwargs

fields.name: use_liger_kernel
fields.help: Enable Liger Kernel optimizations: transformers patches the model's layers with Liger's Triton kernels. Deprecated in `SFTTrainer`, `DPOTrainer`, `KTOTrainer`, `GRPOTrainer` and `RLOOTrainer`, and will be removed in v2.0.0: use `model_init_kwargs={"use_kernels": True}` instead.

fields.name: torch_empty_cache_steps
fields.help: Number of steps to wait before calling `torch.<device>.empty_cache()`. Helps avoid CUDA OOM at a cost of ~10%% slower performance. If None, cache will not be emptied.

fields.name: trust_remote_code
fields.help: Whether to allow loading models and tokenizers that ship custom Python code from the Hub. Forwarded to `AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained` and `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained`.

fields.name: chat_template_path
fields.help: If specified, sets the model's chat template. This can either be the path to a tokenizer (local directory or Hugging Face Hub model) or a direct path to a Jinja template file. fields.name: disable_dropout
fields.help: Whether to disable dropout in the model.

fields.name: dataset_num_proc
fields.help: Number of processes to use for processing the dataset.

fields.name: center_rewards_coefficient
fields.help: Coefficient to incentivize the reward model to output mean-zero rewards (proposed by [this paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2312.09244), Eq. 2). Recommended value: `0.01`.

fields.name: activation_offloading
fields.help: Whether to offload the activations to the CPU.

algorithms.label: SFT
algorithms.summary: RL 之前的冷启动：在指令/补全数据上做监督微调，让模型先具备目标输出格式（如先想再答、带工具调用标记），之后 RL 才容易起量。

stages.model: 策略模型（可叠加 LoRA）。

stages.signal: 监督标签（答案本身）。
stages.rollout: 无。
stages.estimate: 无。

pros: 最稳的起点，几乎不会崩
为后续 RL 提供格式稳定的初版模型

过久会损失探索能力（熵坍缩）
pitfalls: packing=True 时必须确认 attention 掩码正确，否则样本互相污染
